comments.value: I have discovered the exact cause of this issue (It’s the dynamic near distance setting persisting and players not knowing they left it on). This is a very serious design flaw on VRChat’s part which is very easy to fix by letting us override this setting in world.

details:
For some players, if they travel a large distance from origin (~4000 m) THEN travel back to origin, their menu will become very distorted as if by floating point quantization - when they are at origin.

It is important to note that this distortion experienced at origin after the journey has been described as significantly larger than that normally experienced with the menu at ~4000 meters from origin.

I observed some players (~2-3) having this issue in the world Hokyl Night, but one effected player described experiencing something similar in flight worlds that are often similarly large and involve long travel distances in vehicles.

This issue only impacts some players, regardless of avatar size or scale, and is very rare (less than 1/15 players seem to experience this). It has occurred on multiple headset types, all in PCVR. The world in which this has been observed does not use any origin point shifting, but does contain vehicles, but does not use the Sacc system, so I dont think this is a Sacc vehicle issue.

The only thing that I can think of is that the menu somehow acquires a new transform in a manner that is so extreme that it causes it to experience dramatically amplified floating point imprecision larger than it normally would, but only in certain circumstances for some users.

The world in which this was observed (Hokyl Night) does use extremely large-scale meshes for performance and optimization reasons, but it doesn't seem possible that a 2000 meter-wide mesh sitting in a world can do anything to the player’s menu.
title: Menu becomes “jiggly” even after player returns to world origin.
